title: 2017-2019 Super Duty (F-250/350 4x4, F-450/550): steering wheel oscillation after bumps, redesigned steering damper (20N04)
summary: Ford Customer Satisfaction Program 20N04: sustained steering wheel oscillation after hitting rough pavement or an expansion joint, usually above 45 mph. Fix is a redesigned steering linkage damper, covered for 7 years / 100,000 miles. Small vertical play in the drag link and tie rod ends is normal by design.

specs.name: Symptom
specs.value: Sustained steering wheel oscillation after rough pavement or an expansion joint, typically above 45 mph (72 km/h)

specs.name: Extended coverage
specs.value: Steering linkage damper, 7 years or 100,000 miles from warranty start; vehicles already past that were covered through October 31, 2020

specs.name: Normal drag link / tie rod end movement
specs.value: 1-2 mm vertical when pushed or rotated (internal spring design; not a reason to replace)

specs.name: Built
specs.value: Kentucky Truck October 8, 2015 through November 3, 2019; Ohio February 5, 2016 through November 13, 2019

steps.text: Customer reports the steering wheel oscillating after a bump or expansion joint at highway speed.

Replace the steering linkage damper with the redesigned part per Workshop Manual section 211-03, torquing fasteners to the WSM spec. Suspension fasteners are critical; use the same or equivalent parts.
If you inspect the drag link and tie rods, expect 1-2 mm of vertical movement at the ends when pushing or rotating them. That's normal for their internal spring design; don't replace them for it.

body: Ford's term is "sustained steering wheel oscillation"; "death wobble" is only here as a search tag because that's what owners call it. The program covers vehicles that show the condition; it isn't a recall, and Ford had no rental cars approved for it.
